RunPlan checkpoint qualification

contributor-tools-components-runplan-validation-readme.Rmd

Contributing · Object model · Discovery walkthrough · Object fields

Supporting record: claims apply to the revisions and environments named below; this page does not qualify a later candidate.

The source suite passed 189 cases and 4,921 expectations, with no failures, errors, warnings or skips. This snapshot includes the typed RunPlan and its original-payload certificate check. It precedes the requested perturbation-fit cache work.

All seven reference workflows match exactly at tolerance zero across 231 comparisons: actual calibration/power/discovery tables, available preparation values, compact response-fit values, warnings and R RNG state. The archived flat-slot numerical reference uses matched budgets: its accidental calibration B3 overwrite is reset to the prepared discovery/power budget before those runs. This is not a claim of parity with that old overwrite behavior.

source-suite-summary.json contains machine-readable totals; source-suite.log and source-suite-results.rds preserve the full source-suite result. Earlier targeted RunPlan/public-workflow tests are recorded separately as preliminary diagnostics; the final complete suite supersedes that pre-certificate check. parity.log, parity-summary.json, parity-checks.rds and parity-current.rds preserve exact comparison outcomes and current observations. The reference artifact is retained unchanged under ../../schema3/validation/; provenance.json records its hash, all tested source hashes and artifact hashes.

From the repository root, run Rscript tools/components/runplan/validation/run-source-suite.R or Rscript tools/components/runplan/validation/run-parity.R. These scripts require the local compiled native library and developer test dependencies. compare-parity.R can repeat comparison of the saved observations without rerunning workflows. Native samplers and statistical kernels were not modified for this checkpoint. Nextflow adaptation and large-screen performance qualification remain outside this evidence.

Developed by Timothy Barry, Louis Deutsch, Eugene Katsevich, Wharton Analytics, National Science Foundation.
